Regarding the operational processes described in the text, the primary bottleneck is the outdated First-In-First-Out (FIFO) storage system. This system creates inefficiency because newer stock is placed behind older items, making it difficult to access recent inventory. The resulting bottleneck is the time-consuming reorganization effort required every time the latest inventory is needed for shipment. An efficiency improvement would be to implement a more flexible storage system, such as a dynamic slotting system or a warehouse management system that optimizes pick paths, allowing access to newer items without needing to move older stock.
